senses.gloss:
bhoktṛ
(‘the enjoyer,’ or ‘the experiencer’)
------------------------------------------
The two words kartṛ or kartā (‘the doer’) and भोक्तृ or bhoktā (‘the enjoyer,’ ‘the experiencer’) are commonly used in the Hindu philosophical works as applied to the jīvātman (the individual सोउल्). Though the आत्मन् (the Self or the सोउल्) is ever free, how he becomes bound as the jīvātman due to association with अविद्या or अज्ञान (nescience) or प्रकृति (nature) is a question that can never be answered satisfactorily since our मिन्द् which raises this question is itself the product of that nescience.
Once the existence of the jīvātman which is a matter of our common experience is conceded, its corollaries too can be accepted. He is hence both the kartṛ and the भोक्तृ of actions. He experiences the results of all actions done by him. It is this fact of his being a doer and the experiencer of actions and their fruits that results in his bondage leading to rebirth.
Meditation on the आत्मन् as his true Self, which is neither the kartṛ nor the भोक्तृ will ultimately lead to मोक्ष or लिबेरतिओन् from transmigration.
